judgments.reasoning_cat1: The offer terms — title, office, start date, contingency on screenings — are concrete and dated, with the Effective Date expressly defined. Nothing here carries a second reasonable reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is a small internal wrinkle in that the Agreement is void if employment does not begin by March 19, 2013 yet becomes effective only on the last signature (dated March 21), but no other provision turns on that sequencing.
judgments.clause_name: 1. Offer of New Financial Advisor Position

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such instructional materials and other assistance as Wells Fargo Advisors in its sole discretion deems reasonable and necessary" and "complete satisfactorily" are open-textured, though the sole-discretion language largely forecloses argument about the standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Paragraph 5's termination-from-program consequences and Paragraph 4's graduation trigger; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At least initially, you will be eligible for overtime pay" is indefinite as to duration and the salary figure is never stated, and compensation is whatever the Plan says "or as may be otherwise determined ... in its sole discretion." Those are namable soft spots.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4 supplies the end point for overtime eligibility, and Paragraph 8 permits unilateral Plan modification, so the pieces harmonise even if the combination leaves the employee's pay largely discretionary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger (three named licenses plus graduation) and the consequence (title change, monthly draw, loss of overtime eligibility) are stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Paragraph 3's "at least initially" overtime language rather than contradicting it, and the reference to the New FA Compensation Plan for a now-"Financial Advisor" is a minor loose end.
judgments.clause_name: 4. Compensation Upon Graduation From Training Program

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "may lead to consequences, up to and including termination" is vague as to what else it authorises, and "your test dates will extended" is a plain mechanical omission of "be".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 7's at-will policy and with Paragraph 2's program obligations; no operative provision pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated prohibitions (i)–(iv) are precise, but "such other regulatory bodies as Wells Fargo Advisors shall deem necessary or desirable" and the family-member carve-out leave some reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its closing sentence, that the Agreement does not supersede any Wells Fargo HR policies or compliance guidelines, sits in tension with Paragraph 20's declaration that this Agreement is the entire understanding and with Paragraph 8's calling itself a mere synopsis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The at-will language is emphatic and self-contained: either side may end the relationship at any time for any reason, and no other statement can alter it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presses against Paragraph 10(b)(i), which conditions forgiveness of Training Costs on five years of continuous employment, and against the survival of post-employment restrictions in Paragraphs 12 and 15 — a court could be asked whether an at-will employee can be charged for a term he had no right to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Calling the Agreement "only a synopsis of the compensation and other arrangements" is itself an ambiguous characterisation — synopsis of what governing document? — and the proviso exempting all compensation and benefit plans from the no-oral-modification rule is broadly drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in substance with Paragraph 20's "entire understanding" clause and with Paragraph 6's statement that outside policies are not superseded; harmonising "synopsis" with "entire agreement" is not straightforward.
judgments.clause_name: 8. Effect of Agreement; Modification; Entire Agreement

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "fronted" and "deficit balances (unrelated to the offset of the draw)" are undefined shorthand, and "compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors" is an awkward formulation of who earns what.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Paragraph 9(b) and 10(d) on setoff and with the Plan reference; nothing in the Agreement contradicts it, though the Plan itself is not before the reader.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence conditions eligibility on employment "on the date such payments are received by Wells Fargo Advisors" while the last conditions it on employment "on the applicable payout date" — two different dates for the same forfeiture.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Paragraph 9(a)'s promise of "compensation earned and received" before termination, the forfeiture rule is broadly consistent, but the internal date mismatch could be argued against 9(a).
judgments.clause_name: 9(b). Compensation Not Yet Received or Prepaid

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The dollar amounts of the Training Costs are literally blank in the executed document, so the operative quantum of the obligation is missing, and "Based upon your prior experience and qualifications" gives no formula to fill the gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against Paragraph 10(b)'s exceptions and 10(c)'s amortization schedule, and against Paragraph 7's at-will policy; the blank figure makes reconciling 10(a) with 10(c)'s "entire amount" and "1/48 of the total amount" difficult in practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five-year clock and its "later to occur of" trigger are precisely defined; "continuous employment" is the only soft term and is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its five-year measuring period starts at graduation/registration, whereas Paragraph 10(c) amortizes over 48 months starting in the second year of employment as a New FA — the two clocks do not align, and Paragraph 7's at-will rule sits uneasily with a five-year retention condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Competitive Organization or Entity" is defined by a list of named institution types followed by the catch-all "any other person, firm, corporation, or entity that competes with Wells Fargo Advisors" — a classic general-versus-specific scope problem — and "including, but not be limited to" is ungrammatical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Paragraph 10(b)(i) and 10(c) (does joining a competitor in year four revive the whole amortized balance?) and effectively functions as a non-compete alongside the narrower non-solicit in Paragraph 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The office-closure exception is stated with an express clarification that relocation is not a closing, which removes the obvious ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the other 10(b) exceptions and does not collide with any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite — permanent disability or death within the identified five-year period — with only the typographical "identifted".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-references Paragraph 10(b)(i)'s five-year period accurately; the only friction is that 10(c) amortizes over a differently anchored 48 months.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are arithmetically stated but awkward: "reduced by one-forty-eighth ... at the end of each month, beginning with the first month of the second year" leaves the first-year cliff and the 48-month schedule to be pieced together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 48-month amortization anchored to the start of New FA employment does not line up with Paragraph 10(b)(i)'s five-year period anchored to graduation and full registration, so an employee could owe nothing under one clock and something under the other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short setoff permission qualified by "to the maximum extent permitted under applicable law"; the OCR-inserted page number "3" does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the setoff mechanics in Paragraph 9(a) and 13(c) and is consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in "all confidential information or trade secrets ... including, but not limited to" names and telephone numbers and then "all records and other documents made and/or maintained in connection with Wells Fargo Advisors business," so the outer boundary of the defined term is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Paragraphs 11(b), 12 and 14(c) without contradiction; the definition's breadth is a Category 1 issue rather than a clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires surrender of "any Confidential Records or Documents," a term never defined — the defined term in 11(a) is "Confidential Information and Documents" — which is a mechanical mismatch of defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantively it tracks 11(a) and is enforced by 14(c); the term-name slip is the only relational wrinkle and is easily harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any Wells Fargo Advisors client that you had contact with or otherwise learned of" is broad and its edge is uncertain, and "cause or permit to be solicited" imposes a duty of indeterminate scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 10(b)(ii)(A)'s competitor-based reimbursement trigger and with 14(c)'s injunctive carve-out; no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is syntactically broken at the end — "for employment with any other organization ..., or discontinuing his or her employment" has no verb to govern the final clause — and "any other lines of business" is an open catch-all after an enumerated list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 12(a) and is enforceable via 14(c); nothing elsewhere conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "you will be expected to contribute" is not plainly a binding obligation, yet the last sentence calls it "[y]our obligation"; the amount is left to be "determined after a consultation" with management, which fixes no standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 13(c) supplies the collection mechanism and Paragraph 15 the survival, so the scheme hangs together even though the quantum is unilateral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definite prohibitions, but "subject to disciplinary action for trading errors that may have a financial impact on future earnings" is garbled enough that its intended operation is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds directly into 13(c)'s Net Eligible Revenue adjustment and is consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanism is stated definitely; "Net Eligible Revenue" is undefined in this document, and the parenthetical "(i.e., charges spread beyond three (3) months)" defines installment plans somewhat loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the New FA Compensation Plan, which Paragraph 8 lets Wells Fargo modify unilaterally, but that dependence is contemplated rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion list is internally incongruous — NLRA claims are grouped under "claims for State unemployment insurance" via an "i.e." — and the first bullet extends arbitration to disputes with "a client, or any other person," a catch-all whose reach is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is broader than the operative promise in 14(b), which covers only disputes "arising between you and Wells Fargo Advisors," and the carve-outs it announces appear nowhere in 14(b) except by the "[e]xcept as provided in Paragraph 14(c)" reference — a real disclosure-versus-operative-text mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of covered claims ends in "and/or other theory," an unbounded catch-all after enumerated specifics, and the fallback to AAA "Securities Arbitration Rules, effective May 1, 1993" fixes a rule set that may no longer exist; "tortuous" is a misspelling of "tortious."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is narrower than 14(a)'s description (which sweeps in clients and "any other person") and says "[e]xcept as provided in Paragraph 14(c)" while omitting 14(a)'s stated exclusions, so the two subparagraphs of the same clause do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, one-sided but definite carve-out: injunctive relief in any competent court to enforce Paragraphs 11 and 12, with "[n]otwithstanding any other provision" resolving priority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception referenced in 14(b) and is therefore harmonised with the arbitration promise, though its unilateral availability to the employer only invites an equity argument rather than a construction one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survival list uses "including, but not limited to" and names "indemnification obligations," a category that this Agreement never creates, leaving the enumeration mismatched to the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 20's survival sentence covers the same ground in different terms, and the reference to indemnification obligations finds no counterpart anywhere in the Agreement (13(a) speaks of contribution, not indemnity).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence choice of Missouri law expressly excluding conflicts rules; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Choosing Missouri law for a Texas-based employee interacts with the restrictive covenants in 11–13 and with 17's savings clause, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence says invalidity "shall not affect the validity or unenforceability of the remaining Provisions," which is a drafting slip — it should read "or enforceability" — and the reformation-by-court concept is stated loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the restrictive covenants in 11–13 and does not conflict with any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver sentence; the only defect is the OCR artifact "individua!", which does not alter meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the enforcement provisions in 14(c) and the survival provisions; nothing pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is an acknowledgment rather than an obligation, but "THE RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS" is undefined — the reader must guess whether it means Paragraphs 11, 12, 10(b)(ii)(A), or all of them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined label loosely maps onto Paragraphs 11 and 12 and arguably 10(b)(ii)(A)'s competitor condition, but nothing operative depends on resolving the reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "regarding the matters addressed herein" narrows the merger clause in a way whose boundary is uncertain, and the survival sentence is circular — provisions survive if they "require survival ... in order to give full legal effect thereto."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Paragraph 8's statement that the Agreement is "only a synopsis" and Paragraph 6's statement that outside HR and compliance policies are not superseded, and duplicates the survival language of Paragraph 15 in different terms.
